newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lend Lease shares leap to new highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lend Lease shares leap to new highs.

text.p: Shares in property developer and financial services group, Lend Lease Corp Ltd, leapt over three percent to a record high of A$23.80 on Wednesday as investors took an upbeat view on the tightly held company's prospects.
"They have got things on the go," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding the shares were hard to come by.
"The company is one of the prime industrial stocks and is keenly sought after. If you want stock, you just have to pay up."
Brokers said recent announcements had built a strong perception of growth among investors with few sellers to be found.

"There has been a series of anouncements coming out that has built that perception. People have stopped selling," said senior dealer at Burdett, Buckeridge and Young, Stephen Smith, adding that Lend Lease were always looking for ways to strengthen performance.
"They are continually working and engineering the company from within and it is quite obvious the market likes what it's hearing."
Smith cited the Bluewater deal in the UK and the company's more active approach to property development as examples.
"They have gone from passive in the area to proactive and I think the market likes that."
Lend Lease said on November 5 it had signed a A$750 million syndicate of investors for its Bluewater retail development at Kent in southern England.
On November 6, the company said it would have equity participation of US$120 million in a refurbished shopping centre in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania.
On October 31, the company forecast a higher profit in 1996/97 and put a value on its Darling Park commercial property project in Sydney of A$984 million by December 1999.
By 1.55 p.m. (0255 GMT), Lend Lease shares were off early highs but still 59 cents higher on the day at A$23.60 on solid turnover of 504,792 shares.
